displayName: loop-sessions: a machine is behind the published build for a day

conditions.displayName: machines behind the published build at or above 1 for 24 h

documentation.content:
At least one managed laptop is on a sha other than the release manifest's commit a day after it was published. The daemon self-upgrades at its next check, so a machine still behind after a day has not run the check: the laptop was off, the daemon is dead (the silent alert), or the check failed (the `upgrade` block of its health report says why). Builds that are not a release sha (dev, dirty) are counted as unmanaged and never here.

`gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="loop-sessions" AND jsonPayload.message="fleet version_lag"' --freshness=15m --format='value(jsonPayload.email,jsonPayload.agent_version,jsonPayload.published_build,jsonPayload.hours_behind)'`, or the version-lag rows on /admin/fleet with the lag in hours. Ask the person to run `loop-sessions daemon --upgrade-now`, which checks the release host now, ignoring the throttle, and replaces the binary. If the manifest itself is stale (the fleet page's Latest build is older than the server build), publish the release (README 7b).

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-upgrade
